focus: Which flowchart rules survive FigJam, and what replaces the rest
noveltyJustification: Four classifications are new derived claims and two restate prior evidence; the simplicity bonus reflects one three-layer rule model replacing rule-by-rule reasoning.
answeredQuestions: Which sk-design-diagram flow rules carry over to FigJam, and which need a FigJam-native replacement?
ruledOut: Porting the HTML/SVG taste gate wholesale

findings.label: Shape-carries-type survives as intent but not as a verified contract: neither reference enumerates fj shape's accepted shape kinds or flags, so a rectangle/diamond/rounded vocabulary needs --help confirmation.

Four rules are portable unchanged because they are model-level: labelled exits, at most three exits per decision, no colour-encoded node types, and one emphasis colour for the happy path or a single consequential decision.
Three rules are unenforceable in FigJam: the merge dot becomes several edges into one target, the arc jump becomes column placement, and HTML/SVG shape rendering becomes one-node-at-a-time creation.
Top-to-bottom layout stays a rule but becomes costly: move and update are the only positioning verbs, so the pipeline must compute every node position itself.

Edge labelling is the highest-risk rule: if fj connect cannot carry a label, conditions must live as text nodes beside connectors or as suffixes in the target node label, and only the second cannot drift out of alignment.
Enforcement must move with the rules: no FigJam validator exists, so the pipeline needs its own model check for the three-exit ceiling, labelled branches and node-kind vocabulary before any write.
